practices.practice: Keep the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection URI only in an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit it; provide a .env.example with placeholders instead of real secrets.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection URI only in an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit it; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead of the real secret.

practices.practice: Create a single MongoClient/connection instance at app startup and reuse it across the process (do not open a new client per request); set pool-size parameters appropriate to your runtime (e.g., larger maxPoolSize for long-running servers, small pools for serverless).
practices.prior_belief: Create a single MongoClient/connection instance at app startup and reuse it everywhere (do not open a new connection per request); set an appropriate maxPoolSize (e.g., maxPoolSize=50) in the connection options.

practices.practice: Always connect with TLS (tls=true / ssl=true) and verify certificates; do not disable TLS in production or log connection strings that have TLS disabled.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL on the connection (ssl=true / tls=true) and verify certificates; do not disable TLS in production or log connection strings with tls flags turned off.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using MongoDB Shell
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB TLS required connection string

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) / RBAC or other short-lived credentials over long-lived account keys and avoid baking primary keys into source control or configs.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer managed identity / Azure AD or short-lived credentials to long-lived account keys when possible; avoid baking primary keys into app configuration or source control.

practices.practice: Restrict cluster access with network controls: use IP firewall rules and/or Private Endpoint / VNet service endpoints so only authorized hosts can reach the DocumentDB cluster.
practices.prior_belief: Restrict cluster access with network controls: use IP firewall rules and/or VNet service endpoints/private link so only the app host(s) can reach the DocumentDB cluster.

practices.practice: When loading or seeding many documents, use bulk-write / insertMany (optionally unordered) or SDK bulk modes, and consider creating indexes after ingestion to improve throughput; use upserts or unique keys for idempotent seeds.
practices.prior_belief: When loading or seeding many documents, use bulk writes (insertMany with ordered:false or bulkWrite) and tune writeConcern (e.g., { w:1 }) to improve throughput and to make seeding idempotent use upsert or unique eventId keys.
practices.source_name: Tips for optimizing vector indexing & Insert multiple documents
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB insertMany bulk insert best practices

practices.practice: Create a compound index for the timeline query pattern, e.g., { customerId: 1, timestamp: 1 }, so per-customer sorting by timestamp can be served by an index.
practices.prior_belief: Create a compound index to support the common timeline query pattern, e.g., { customerId: 1, timestamp: 1 } (and include channel as a second or covered field if you filter/sort by it) so per-customer sorting by timestamp is index-backed.

practices.practice: In aggregation pipelines, place $match and $sort as early as possible and ensure sort fields are covered by an index (follow ESR: Equality → Sort → Range when designing compound indexes).
practices.prior_belief: For aggregation pipelines, put $match and $sort stages as early as possible and ensure the sort fields are covered by an index; prefer pipelines like [{$match: {...}}, {$sort: {timestamp:1}}, {$group: {...}}].

practices.practice: Project only required fields in find() or aggregation to reduce RU consumption and network transfer (e.g., { timestamp:1, channel:1, eventType:1, metadata:1 }).
practices.prior_belief: Use projection to return only required fields (e.g., { timestamp:1, channel:1, eventType:1, metadata:1 }) to reduce RU consumption and network transfer in both aggregation and find queries.

practices.practice: Validate index usage and query shape with explain('executionStats') for representative queries/pipelines and tune indexes or pipeline shape until the plan shows index scans rather than COLLSCAN.
practices.prior_belief: Validate index usage with explain() (executionStats) for representative aggregation pipelines and tune indexes or pipeline shape until the explain shows index scans rather than COLLSCAN.

practices.practice: Build vector indexes on a dedicated vector field with fixed dimensionality and explicit index parameters (choose DiskANN/HNSW/IVF per scale) and make index creation idempotent in scripts.
practices.prior_belief: Build vector indexes only on a dedicated vector field with a fixed dimensionality and explicit index parameters (e.g., index type HNSW with specific M and efConstruction or DiskANN parameters) and ensure the index creation script is idempotent.

practices.practice: Normalize and record vector dimensionality and, when using cosine similarity, store normalized (unit-length) embeddings at insert time so similarity comparisons are consistent.
practices.prior_belief: Normalize or fix vector dimensionality and, if using cosine similarity, normalize vectors (unit length) at insert time so vector comparisons are consistent and the index behaves correctly.

practices.practice: When combining metadata filters with vector search, pre-filter by metadata (pass a filter to cosmosSearch) so the vector search runs over a smaller candidate set and preserves recall while reducing RU and latency.
practices.prior_belief: When combining metadata filters with vector search, pre-filter by metadata (e.g., $match customerId and channel) and then run the vector search on the smaller set (hybrid filtering) to reduce RU cost and improve latency.
practices.source_name: Use LangChain on Azure with Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector pre-filter metadata guidance

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors and explicitly handle 429 (throttling) by honoring Retry-After and retrying after that delay.
practices.prior_belief: Implement exponential backoff retries on transient errors (network failures, timeouts) and explicitly handle 429/RU-throttling responses by reading Retry-After headers and retrying after that delay.

practices.practice: Monitor RU/s consumption, latency, and throttling for typical aggregations and provision or autoscale throughput so heavy aggregations or vector searches are not routinely throttled.
practices.prior_belief: Plan throughput: monitor RU/s consumption for typical aggregations and provision/scale throughput (or use autoscale) so heavy aggregations or vector searches are not throttled during normal operation.

practices.practice: Avoid unbounded in-memory aggregation ($group that accumulates huge arrays); stream results, page by timestamp ranges, or use $limit and incremental aggregation to keep memory usage bounded.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid unbounded memory operations in aggregation ($group that builds huge arrays); instead stream results, page by timestamp range, or use $limit and incremental aggregation to keep working set bounded.

practices.practice: Create unique indexes (e.g., on eventId) to make seed scripts idempotent so re-running them can upsert or ignore duplicates safely.
practices.prior_belief: Create unique indexes for idempotency (e.g., unique index on eventId) so seed scripts can upsert or ignore duplicates safely when re-run.

practices.practice: Use allowDiskUse: true for aggregation pipelines that require large sorts or groupings so the engine can spill to disk instead of failing or exhausting memory (and measure RU impact).
practices.prior_belief: Use allowDiskUse: true for aggregation pipelines that require large sorts or groupings so queries can spill to disk instead of failing or using excessive memory, and measure RU impact.

practices.practice: Use cursor.batchSize and server-side cursors for large result sets and prefer range-based (timestamp > lastSeen) or cursor-based pagination over skip-based pagination for timeline queries.
practices.prior_belief: Use cursor.batchSize and server-side cursors for large result sets and avoid skip-based pagination for timelines; prefer range-based pagination on timestamp (e.g., timestamp > lastSeen) to keep performance predictable.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB pagination guidance skip vs cursor

practices.practice: Instrument and monitor RU consumption, latency, index usage, connection pool usage and 429s; use those metrics to tune indexes, queries and throughput.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and monitor: collect metrics for RU consumption, latency, index usage, connection pool utilization and 429s; use those metrics to adjust indexes, queries and throughput.

practices.practice: Make index creation idempotent in startup/infra scripts (use createIndexes with the same specification) and avoid building indexes on very large collections during peak production traffic.
practices.prior_belief: Make index creation idempotent in startup/infra scripts (use createIndexes with the exact same specification) and avoid creating indexes on very large collections during peak production traffic without scheduling maintenance.

practices.practice: Avoid large $lookup or cross-collection joins for per-customer timelines; denormalize frequently-read event metadata into the event document to make timeline aggregation simpler and indexable.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid large $lookup or cross-collection joins in pipelines for per-customer timelines; denormalize frequently-read event metadata into the event document to make the timeline aggregation simpler and indexable.

practices.practice: Protect secrets and telemetry: never log full connection strings or primary keys; mask or omit secrets in error messages and telemetry sent to logs or APM.
practices.prior_belief: Protect secrets and telemetry: never log the full connection string or primary keys; mask or omit secrets in error messages and telemetry sent to logs or APM.

practices.practice: Before using features like retryable writes or multi-document transactions, verify the cluster's supported MongoDB wire protocol version and feature support rather than assuming full MongoDB parity.
practices.prior_belief: If the MongoDB wire protocol version or features (retryable writes, transactions) are needed, verify the cluster wire version and supported features before using them; do not assume full MongoDB parity.
practices.source_name: Azure DocumentDB at a glance (MongoDB compatibility)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB compatibility MongoDB wire versions

practices.practice: Add TTL indexes on ephemeral event collections (createIndex on a date field with expireAfterSeconds) to automatically reclaim storage for time-limited event data.
practices.prior_belief: Add TTL indexes on ephemeral event collections (e.g., session traces) to reclaim storage automatically (createIndex({ createdAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: N })) where appropriate.

practices.practice: Prefer Azure DocumentDB's textSearch + $search and the service's search indexes over the community $text index for production text search use cases.

Choose vector index algorithm by scale: prefer DiskANN for large production corpora, HNSW for medium datasets (~up to 50k), and IVF for small datasets; tune lBuild/lSearch, maxDegree and consider product quantization or fp16 to reduce memory.
For large bulk ingestion, consider enabling SDK bulk modes or parallelized ingestion (or create indexes after ingestion) to reduce write amplification and improve throughput.
